dissents.topic: Pinning setuptools<82 as a runtime dependency in core/setup.py

positions.position: Adding setuptools<82 to core extras is a quick, targeted way to keep CI green and ensure downstream users don't hit the pkg_resources removal when using the mmcv extra. It is annotated as a FIXME and can be removed when upstream is patched.

setuptools<82 is being added to a generic extras_require block (the diff context suggests it ends up applied broadly), not scoped to the mmcv/mmdet extra. This pins setuptools globally for users who don't need mmcv at all, propagating an upstream MMCV bug into AutoGluon's public install constraints.

The PR's stated goal is fixing the setuptools/pkg_resources breakage. Bumping mmdet to 3.3.0 is an unrelated version change with no justification in the description; it should be split out or justified.

mmdet 3.3.0 may be required for compatibility with the PyPI mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0 combination now that the git-pinned mmengine is gone. Bundling the bump is reasonable to land a known-good matrix.

issues.description: setuptools<82 added to core extras_require, not scoped to mmcv-only users
issues.detail: The new 'setuptools<82' constraint is added inside an extras_require entry in core/setup.py. Pinning setuptools as a runtime dependency for users of AutoGluon core (or of whichever extra this block represents) propagates an upstream MMCV bug to users who never install mmcv/mmdet. The cap should at minimum be confined to the multimodal/mmcv-specific extra, and ideally kept out of installed dependencies entirely (it's a build-time concern handled in the CI scripts).

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation without ensuring full build deps are present
issues.detail: setup_mmcv.sh now runs `pip install "mmcv==2.1.0" --no-build-isolation`. With build isolation disabled, mmcv's setup.py runs against whatever is in the ambient environment. The script installs setuptools<82 first but does not explicitly ensure wheel, torch, ninja, or numpy at compatible versions are present before the build, which can produce fragile or non-reproducible CI builds depending on the base image.

issues.description: Unrelated mmdet version bump (3.2.0 -> 3.3.0) bundled into a CI fix PR
issues.detail: The PR's stated purpose is to fix the mmengine/setuptools failure, but it also bumps mmdet from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no justification in the description. Version bumps of detection stacks can shift model APIs, configs, and weights compatibility; this change should either be justified (e.g., required for mmengine 0.10.7 compatibility) or split into its own PR.

issues.description: Install order in setup_mmcv.sh installs mmcv before mmengine
issues.detail: The script installs mmcv==2.1.0 before mmengine==0.10.7. mmcv depends on mmengine at runtime; pip will typically resolve and pull in some mmengine during the mmcv install, which may not match the explicit 0.10.7 you intend. Installing mmengine first (or pinning both in a single pip invocation) would make the resolved versions deterministic.

issues.description: Switch from `mim install` to `pip install` for mmcv loses prebuilt wheel selection
issues.detail: Previously `mim install mmcv==2.1.0` was used, which selects an OpenMMLab-hosted prebuilt wheel matched to the local torch/CUDA. Switching to `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` is more likely to trigger a source build, increasing CI time and the chance of compile failures. The FIXME comment acknowledges this is temporary, which is fine, but worth tracking explicitly.

issues.description: FIXME comments reference the same upstream issue in two places without a tracking owner/date
issues.detail: Two FIXMEs cite open-mmlab/mmcv#3325. Without an internal tracking issue or owner, these caps tend to ossify. Consider linking an internal ticket or adding a TODO with a target date to revisit.

issues.description: build_pkg pins setuptools<82 in CI build environment, may mask issues with newer setuptools in user installs
issues.detail: Capping setuptools<82 during sdist/bdist_wheel build is a reasonable CI workaround, but the produced wheels are built against an older setuptools while end-users may use setuptools>=82. This is usually harmless for pure-Python wheels but worth noting; once mmcv#3325 is fixed, the cap should be removed promptly to avoid divergence.

review.summary: The PR works around an upstream MMCV/mmengine incompatibility with setuptools>=82 (pkg_resources removal) by capping setuptools in CI build scripts and switching mmengine/mmcv/mmdet installations from a git-pinned mmengine + mim install to direct PyPI installs with --no-build-isolation. The CI-script changes are reasonable as temporary workarounds and are well-commented with FIXMEs pointing at mmcv#3325. The main concern is core/setup.py adding setuptools<82 to extras_require, which pushes a CI-level build constraint into a user-facing dependency; this should be scoped to the mmcv/multimodal extra or removed. Secondary concerns: an unrelated mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 bump bundled into a bug-fix PR, install ordering (mmcv before mmengine), and loss of mim's prebuilt-wheel matching when switching to plain pip with --no-build-isolation. No P0 blockers, but P1 cleanup is warranted before merge.
